rounds.text: Polyplex Corporation Ltd trades at a highly attractive valuation, with a price-to-book ratio of 0.70x against a book value of ₹ 1,415 [E2], and a compelling P/E ratio of just 7.57x compared to a sector benchmark of 21.1x [E6]. This deep discount is further emphasized by a low EV/EBITDA of 3.66x versus the sector benchmark of 12.1x [E11]. Fundamental momentum is accelerating sharply, highlighted by a trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth of 16% [E17] and a staggering 215% compounded profit growth over the same period [E21], alongside a quarterly operating margin expanding to 12% in Sep 2026 compared to 6% a year ago [E31]. Cash generation is exceptionally robust, demonstrated by a Mar 2026 operating cash flow of Rs 537 Cr and a cash conversion ratio of 13.10x, ensuring reported profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests a material margin of safety of 33.0% at the current market price of ₹ 987 [E45, E46]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor historical sales and profit growth over 3 and 5-year periods, along with low multi-year return on equity figures [E16, E19, E20, E27, E28, E63].

The fundamental profitability of the business fails to support its valuation, evidenced by a dismal return on equity of 1.4% [E13] and an ROCE of just 0.9% [E12], alongside a low median ROE of 1% over the last year [E29]. Long-term wealth destruction is apparent through a 5-year compounded profit growth of -36% [E19] and a 3-year compounded sales contraction of -3% [E16], paired with a 5-year share price return of -10% [E23]. Balance sheet health faces rising pressures as borrowings climbed to Rs 1,219 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 935 Cr a year prior [E39], alongside a massive 437.1% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 376 Cr [E40] that flags active, unproven capex risks, further aggravated by a flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E64]. Promoter alignment is notably weak with a low holding of 26.7% [E62], which has decreased over the last 3 years by -24.2% [E65], accompanied by negative institutional money flow (-0.31 percentage points) [E44]. Relative price weakness is confirmed by a relative-strength rating of only 36 against the Nifty 500 [E51] and a severe historical drawdown of -76.3% [E53]. Conceded: [E21] and [E35].

The bear focuses heavily on low trailing ROE and ROCE figures [E12, E13, E29], but ignores the profound operational turnaround already underway where TTM profit growth surged by 215% [E21], operating margins expanded by 4 percentage points in TTM [E30] and by 6 percentage points in the most recent quarter [E31], and sales grew by 16% over the trailing twelve months [E17]. While borrowings increased [E39] and capital work-in-progress rose [E40], this reflects an active growth spend and capex build-up phase [E40] backed by comfortable short-term liquidity with a current ratio of 2.59x [E38] and robust cash generation where operating cash flow reached Rs 537 Cr [E35] with profits fully backed by cash conversion of 13.10x [E34]. Conceded: [E16, E19, E23, E44, E51, E53, E62, E64, E65]. The dramatic acceleration in net profit up 429% YoY [E69] and improving results scoring 100/100 demonstrate that stale backward-looking metrics miss the fundamental inflection happening right now [E74]. Furthermore, trading at a steep discount with a price-to-book ratio of 0.70x [E2] and an EV/EBITDA of 3.66x against a sector benchmark of 12.1x [E11] offers a massive margin of safety that more than compensates for past cyclical weakness.

Conceded: [E21, E30, E31, E35]. The bull relies on short-term operational improvements while ignoring chronic, structural weakness across profitability metrics, such as a multi-year ROCE of 0.9% and ROE of 1.4% [E12, E13], alongside a 3-year median ROE of just 3% [E28]. The low promoter holding of 26.7% and a sharp 24.2% decrease in promoter stake over the last 3 years signal weak insider commitment [E62, E65], paired with institutional money flow registering negative [E44]. Furthermore, the massive 437.1% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 376 Cr alongside rising borrowings of Rs 1,219 Cr [E39, E40] carries the explicit risk that the company might be capitalizing the interest cost [E64]. The bull's invocation of a deep price-to-book discount [E2] ignores the historical context of a severe peak-to-trough drawdown of -76.3% [E53] and a weak relative-strength rating of 36 [E51].
